- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot early in upward trends.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.30) — model fails to capture sharp downside momentum.
- Lag in price corrections: model often delays reaction to sentiment shifts, especially after strong spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp rallies, leading to premature peaks followed by overcorrections.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., 2024-12-18) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- Avoid extrapolating recent momentum if sentiment is mixed or trending sideways — model overfits recent volatility.
- When sentiment is trending upward but price is flat, model tends to project a steep rise — adjust downward if sentiment is not strong enough to justify.
- Don’t assume sentiment directly translates to price — model often ignores sentiment decay or reversal signals.
